en: Thus have I heard: the Sāleyyaka Sutta, the forty-first discourse of the Majjhima Nikāya.
On one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on tour among the Kosalans with a large community of monks, he arrived at a brahmin village of the Kosalans named Sālā.
The brahmin householders of Sālā heard:
"Friends, the ascetic Gotama—the son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan—is wandering on tour among the Kosalans with a large community of monks and has arrived at Sālā."
Furthermore, this excellent reputation has spread concerning the venerable Gotama:

"Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant, perfectly enlightened, endowed with clear vision and virtuous conduct, sublime, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.
Having personally realized this world—with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—through direct knowledge, he makes it known.
He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing;
he reveals the holy life, entirely complete and pure.
It is indeed good to see such Arahants.”
Then the brahmin householders of Sālā approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side;
some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and having concluded the courteous and amiable conversation, sat down to one side; some... [sat down to one side].
They extended their joined palms toward the Blessed One and sat down to one side;
some, having announced their names and clans in the presence of the Blessed One, sat down to one side; and some sat down to one side in silence.
Seated to one side, the brahmin householders of Sālā addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Master Gotama, what is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, perdition, even in hell?
And what, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world?”

“Householders, it is because of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, perdition, even in hell.
Householders, it is because of righteous conduct and proper conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
“We do not understand in detail the meaning of what Master Gotama has spoken in brief, which has not been explained in detail. [Please explain it to us.]”

“It would be well if Master Gotama would teach us the Dhamma in such a way that we might understand in detail the meaning of what he has spoken in brief, without having explained the meaning in detail.
“In that case, householders, listen and attend closely; I shall speak.
“Yes, sir,” the brahmin householders of Sālā replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:

“Householders, there are three kinds of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct by way of body, four kinds of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct by way of speech, and three kinds of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct by way of mind.
And how, householders, are there three kinds of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct by way of body?”
In this case, householders, a certain person is a destroyer of life: he is cruel, bloody-handed, intent on killing and striking, and lacks compassion for living beings.

Furthermore, he is a taker of what is not given: whatever belongs to another, whether it be the property or belongings of another found in a village or in the wilderness, he takes it by means of theft.
Moreover, he engages in sexual misconduct: he has intercourse with women who are protected by their mother, protected by their father, or protected by both parents...
One who engages in sexual misconduct with women protected by their mother, protected by their father, protected by their relatives, protected by their clan, protected by the Dhamma,
those who have a husband, those who are under threat of punishment, or even those who are merely surrounded by a circle of flowers—
in such cases, he engages in improper conduct. In this way, householders, there is threefold unrighteous and irregular conduct by way of the body.
And how, householders, is there fourfold unrighteous conduct and improper conduct by way of speech?

Here, householders, a certain person is a speaker of falsehood. Whether in an assembly, or in a gathering, or in the midst of kinsmen, or in the midst of a guild, or in the presence of the royal court, being summoned and questioned as a witness: "Come now, good man..."
‘Tell me what you know. Not knowing, he says, ‘I know’; or knowing, he says, ‘I do not know.
Not seeing, he says, ‘I see’; or seeing, he says, ‘I do not see. Thus, for his own sake, or for the sake of another, or for the sake of some small material gain, he speaks a deliberate lie.
Moreover, he is one who speaks divisively. Having heard something here, he reports it there for the sake of dividing these people;

or having heard something there, he reports it here for the sake of dividing those people. Thus, he is a divider of those who are united, or a promoter of division among those who are already divided.
He delights in discord, rejoices in discord, finds pleasure in discord, and utters speech that causes discord.

Furthermore, he is harsh in speech. He utters such speech as is cutting, rough, bitter, insulting to others, provocative of anger, and conducive to lack of concentration. Furthermore, he is a frivolous talker.

He speaks at the wrong time, speaks what is untrue, speaks what is useless, speaks contrary to the Dhamma, and speaks contrary to the Vinaya. He utters speech that is not worth treasuring—speech spoken at the wrong time, without foundation, incoherent, and unbeneficial.
In this way, householders, there is a fourfold unrighteous and improper conduct regarding speech.
And how, householders, is there a threefold unrighteous and improper conduct by way of the mind?
Here, householders, a certain person is covetous; he covets the wealth and possessions of others, thinking: "O, that what belongs to another were mine!
Furthermore, he has a mind of ill will and corrupt intentions, thinking: "May these beings be slain, or destroyed, or cut off, or annihilated, or may they not exist at all!"
Moreover, he holds wrong view and possesses perverted vision:
"There is no giving, there is no sacrifice, there is no offering; there is no fruit or result of deeds well done or ill done;
there is no this world, there is no other world; there is no mother, there is no father; there are no beings..."
‘There are no recluses or brahmins in the world who have attained the right path, who practice rightly, and who,
having realized this world and the other world for themselves through direct knowledge, make them known.
In this way, householders, there is a threefold unrighteous and improper conduct by means of the mind.

"Thus, householders, it is because of unrighteous conduct and improper conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.
Now, householders, righteous conduct and proper conduct are threefold by way of body, fourfold by way of speech, and threefold by way of mind.
And how, householders, is righteous conduct and proper conduct threefold by way of body?"

In this case, householders, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from taking life. Laying aside the rod and laying aside the weapon, being conscientious and compassionate, he dwells sympathetic toward the welfare of all living beings.

Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. Whatever belongs to another, whether it be in a village or in the forest, he does not take it by way of theft when it has not been given.
Having abandoned sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct. As for those women who are protected by their mother, protected by their father...
One does not engage in sexual misconduct with women protected by their mother, father, parents, brother, sister, relatives, clan, or Dhamma;
those who have a husband, those who are under threat of punishment, or even those merely encircled by a flower garland—with such women one does not commit unchastity.
In this way, householders, there is threefold righteous conduct and harmonious conduct by way of the body.
And how, householders, is there fourfold righteous conduct and peaceful conduct in speech?
Here, householders, a certain person, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech.
Whether in an assembly, or in a council, or in the midst of kinsmen, or in the midst of a guild, or in the royal court, when summoned...
When questioned as a witness, saying: "Come now, good man, speak what you know," he says, "I do not know," if he does not know;
he says, "I know," if he knows; he says, "I do not see," if he does not see; or he says, "I see," if he sees.
Thus, whether for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of some small material gain, he does not speak a conscious lie.
Having abandoned malicious speech, he abstains from malicious speech.

Having heard something here, he does not repeat it elsewhere for the purpose of dividing those people; nor, having heard something there, does he repeat it here for the purpose of dividing these people.

Thus, he is a reconciler of those who are divided and a promoter of harmony among those who are united. Delighting in concord, rejoicing in concord, finding joy in concord, he speaks words that create concord.

Having abandoned harsh speech, he abstains from harsh speech. He speaks such words as are gentle, pleasing to the ear, endearing, heart-warming, polite, agreeable to many people, and dear to many people.
Having abandoned idle chatter, he abstains from idle chatter. He speaks at the proper time, speaks what is true, speaks what is beneficial, speaks on the Dhamma, speaks on the Vinaya;
he speaks words that are worth treasuring, delivered at the right time, accompanied by reason, measured, and connected with the goal.
In this way, householders, there is fourfold righteous conduct and peaceful conduct by way of speech.
And how, householders, is there threefold righteous conduct and peaceful conduct by way of mind?
Here, householders, a certain person is not covetous; he does not covet the wealth and possessions of others, thinking: "O, that what belongs to another were mine!"

Moreover, he is one whose mind is uncorrupted and whose mental intentions are not malignant, thinking: “May these beings be free from enmity, free from affliction, free from distress, and may they maintain themselves in happiness.
Furthermore, he possesses right view and undistorted vision, [thinking]:
“There is what is given, there is what is sacrificed, there is what is offered; there is the fruit and result of deeds well done and ill done.”
‘This world exists; the other world exists; there is mother and father; there are beings of spontaneous birth;

and there are in this world ascetics and brahmins who have fared rightly and practiced rightly, who have realized for themselves through direct knowledge this world and the other world and make them known.’”
In this way, householders, there is a threefold practice of Dhamma and right conduct by means of the mind.
It is because of this practice of Dhamma and right conduct, householders, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
If a practitioner of Dhamma and right conduct should desire:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of wealthy kṣatriyas!’—
it is indeed possible that, after the breakup of the body, after death, he will be reborn in the company of wealthy kṣatriyas. And why is that?
For he is one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma, should wish:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the wealthy brahmins... [and so on].
‘May I be reborn in the company of wealthy householders’—
it is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he will be reborn in the company of wealthy householders. And why is that?
For he is one who lives by the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives by the Dhamma and lives righteously should wish:
"Oh, that upon the dissolution of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings," [it would be so].
It is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he might be reborn in the company of the Cātumahārājika devas.
And why is that? Because he is one who conducts himself according to the Dhamma and conducts himself with equanimity.
Householders, if a practitioner of the Dhamma, one who lives righteously, should wish:
"Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the Tāvatiṃsa gods...
[or] among the Yāma gods..."
...of the Tusita devas ...
of the Nimmānarati devas ...
of the Paranimmitavasavatti devas ...
‘May I be reborn in companionship with the devas of Brahma’s company’—
it is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body, after death, he will be reborn in companionship with the devas of Brahma’s company. And why is that?
For such a person is one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives with equanimity.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and with equanimity should wish:
"Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might arise in the company of the Ābhassara devas! [then it will come to pass].
It is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he might be reborn in the company of the Ābhā devas.
And why is that? Because he is one who conducts himself according to the Dhamma and conducts himself with equanimity.
Householders, if one who lives by the Dhamma and lives righteously should wish:
"O, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might [be reborn] among the gods of Limited Radiance...
[or] among the gods of Immeasurable Radiance..."
...of the Ābhassara devas ...
of the Parittasubha devas ...
of the Appamāṇasubha devas ...
...of the Subhakiṇha devas ...
of the Vehapphala devas ...
of the Aviha devas ...
...of the Atappa devas...
of the Sudassa devas...
of the Sudassi devas...
...of the Akaniṭṭha devas ...
of the devas who have reached the base of infinite space ...
of the devas who have reached the base of infinite consciousness ...
‘May I arise in companionship with the devas who have reached the base of nothingness… or the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception’—
it is indeed possible that, with the breakup of the body after death, he will arise in companionship with the devas who have reached the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
For what reason?
Because he is one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously.
Householders, if one who lives according to the Dhamma and lives righteously should so desire:
‘O, that by the destruction of the taints, I might dwell having realized for myself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom,

and having attained them, abide therein!’— it is indeed possible that he, by the destruction of the taints, might dwell having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained them, abide therein. And why is that?
"For he is one who lives according to the Dhamma, one who lives in accordance with the Dhamma.
When this was said, the brahmin householders of Sālā said to the Blessed One:
"Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama!"
"Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden,
or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—
just so has the Dhamma been elucidated by Master Gotama in many ways."
“We, sir, go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
May Master Gotama accept us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.
The Sāleyyaka Sutta, the first, is finished.
